"Have I told you about the time he once personally gifted me a bouquet of flowers?" Laughter snuck through Mydeimos as he recalled that priceless scene. "The look on his face when I explained its meaning..."

"My word..."

"He meant no harm by it." Phainon had merely been issuing his own traditions, was all, "but his reaction will remain in my memory till eternal death."

"Of all the indignity..." Krateros shook his head, much like a disapproving elder who had witnessed a hilarious, blasphemous scene. "And you still deem him a worthy equal—nay, a suitor, Mydeimos?"

What a strange and weighted question. "And what if I do?"

There is no word for 'love' in the Kremnoan language, but there are alternatives.

chapters.html:
If there was one thing Mydeimos knew about Phainon, it was that he craved touch like a starving man yearned for bread. Whether it came through a mere brush of their shoulders, a fleeting graze of fingers against gauntlets, or even a brazen embrace taken in public, the Deliverer was hardly ever shy in declaring his needs.

It had only gotten more prevalent as of late. What used to be brief instances of touch had become a lingering hand on Mydeimos' person, or a longing gaze held throughout casual conversation. He was not unsettled by it—he was much too used to Phainon's eccentricities by now—however, the prince would be lying if he claimed he was not... overwhelmed at times. For all the Deliverer's nickname may imply, he was as passionate as the sun he bore on his neck. Few could even hope to look upon him for long, lest they risked becoming swallowed by his fiery compassion.

The nickname "Snowy" was merely superficial.

Were Mydeimos not his equal, he might turn away from that fool's unwavering personality in battle, in the baths, and in their bedchambers. Titans only knew how affectionate Phainon could be out in public; they knew not his unquenchable need to latch onto Mydeimos the moment the doors shut behind them.

At present, the prince found himself spending his rest day in the kitchens. The warmth of the furnace set his muscles at ease, just as the salty brine of the seafood carried its familiar scent. Mydeimos set his chalice down and returned to the stove where the pans sizzled away. Even the odd splattering of oil against his arms deterred him not from finishing the rest of the cooking.

He was alone today, with neither duties to fulfil nor an errand to run. Phainon just so happened to be busy helping out his strange professor in the Garden of Life for... a lecture on the natural behaviours of dromas, if the prince was not mistaken. There will be time to meet the Deliverer yet—long after an early rise spent nestled together in his bed. For now, there was lunch to be made for the Kremnoan Detachment before the coming Lucid Hour.

Rare were the times when his clansmen would gather together in one place, to indulge in a familiar atmosphere without concern for judgement. Goblets were kept filled with ripe pomegranate juice, plates piled high with dishes fit for the Kremnoan palette, and the belting chatter was understood only by their native ears.

Every face was a dearly familiar one. Be it the men, the women, the children, or the elderly, Mydeimos knew his kin as well as a lion recognised its pride. The armour donned by every Kremnoan warrior was fitted like a part of their very bodies, their attires embroidered in gold amidst a canvas of flowing cottons and sandals. Many wore jewellery, yet few were intricate...

Mydeimos swirled his chalice as the feast continued on. It was only when he noticed footsteps approaching his back did he think to turn his heel.

"Ah, Krateros. I see you have joined us today."

His old teacher, an esteemed warrior crowned in honour. His age was carried with great dignity, especially among their fellow clansmen.

"As if I would miss such an event," Krateros huffed. "To find you organising a gathering is a rare enough occasion as it is. I would rather spend my time here than with the ignorant locals of this city, anyway."

"Is that so? I seem to recall your distinct absence during our last feast," and, be it left unsaid, the reason was due to a certain snow-laden fool, was it not?

Another huff, though it lacked much vitriol—just enough for a weathered man of his age to appear sour. "That boy has quite the determination, I'll admit. His stubbornness even reminds me of yourself, Mydeimos."

Well, that was a given. Phainon had been rather persistent with his advances—if anything, he still was—and he was never one to be deterred by obliviousness.

"Fortunately, his strength has earned my highest regard," Mydeimos said. He would not tolerate any less from his would-be partner. The many weeks of their budding relationship had not been unpleasant, and the prince had learned much of Phainon's personality behind the facade he so often wore.

His cheerfulness was a bubbling warmth, his smile always a dear sight. The Deliverer was never shy with compliments, either, despite his acknowledgment of flattery holding little meaning to a Kremnoan's ears.

Always a bundle of joy, that fool. Phainon was easy to please, and he was tactful to never cause Mydeimos any purposeful discomfort. He was kind, compassionate, and sweet as a ripened pomegranate, a commendable warrior with a heart of pure gold.

Krateros must have sensed the esteem with which Mydeimos spoke of Amphoreus' Deliverer, for he lightened his tone to one of curiosity instead. "I see he has met your standards, then... Regardless of his swordsmanship, there also lies the mystery of his lineage. Aedes Elysiae, was it? A village from the outer lands. Is it not suspicious that no one has heard tale of it before?"

Perhaps. Mydeimos had indeed wondered about that elusive village many a time. It was natural to wonder, after all, even if Phainon hardly ever mentioned his birthplace unprompted.

"Let's not speak of him," the prince said. He raised his chalice to Krateros for a toast instead. "We are amongst our people, and our conversations shall be held at present. Take a seat, teacher. I will fetch some oysters."

The gathering continued without a pause. Apart from the occasional bows and greetings Mydeimos received, he was not approached for questions or needless chatter. Though he donned the crown as prince of Castrum Kremnos, he did not exert his status, nor did he exude authority over his fellow clansmen. Such a feast as this was meant to be relaxing, after all. There will be no incident under his watch.

The table in which Krateros sat gave a pleasant view of the gardens through the windows. Odd nymphs fluttered by with the invisible breeze, just as the colourful plants swayed to its whims. It was there where Mydeimos brought his old teacher his share of the meal; a plate of fresh oysters from a crate of ice, a chalice of juice, a bowl of steaming avgolemono, a generous serving of sliced bread...

Even Krateros was amused by the spread laid before him. "Pomegranate juice lightened with goat milk, as always. Your tastes have yet to change."

"You have never complained," Mydeimos said. He raised his own chalice—one he had already refilled—with a tempered smile. "Besides, one must take on the duty of serving their elders a meal on occasion."

"Hmph. Calling me old?"

"Yes."

A long, exasperated sigh, but the warrior's beard betrayed his smile.

"Children these days... lacking both respect for their superiors, and tact." It was said in jest, of course. Krateros bore thicker skin than the Council Elders of the holy city. He simply accepted the proffered drink without argument, raising it in toast before he took an idle sip.

When he next picked up his fork, he had only one other question. "How have you been, Mydeimos?"

"Quite well." 

"Hmm. You seem happier."

Happier? "In what way?" Mydeimos asked.

The old warrior glanced upon him, taking another long dreg of his drink whilst humming toward himself.

"That boy," he began only afterwards, "I have spotted the both of you amongst each other's presence quite often as of late. I take it, then, that you believe he is a decent match despite his peculiarities? You would not be entertaining him otherwise."

How dull. The prince sighed, "I have said to not speak of him."

"But it is a matter of importance," Krateros remarked. "After all, this is not your first affair, and we Kremnoans do not devote ourselves to any soul. For that boy to have earned your praise, he must have truly impressed you so, in spite of your reservations. I fail to see what he possesses that his fellow Heirs might not."

And since when was Krateros such an observant man in regards to love? Such a word didn't even exist in the Kremnoan dictionary, yet he recognised the undying passion Phainon bore for Mydeimos. Perhaps it was the Deliverer's persistence which conveyed his feelings, for there was little else Mydeimos could imagine which may convince Krateros. The old warrior was rather protective, and he always held a critical eye against outsiders.

If it were affirmations he sought, then he shall have it. At the very least, Phainon deserved to not have his name besmirched. 

"He is a dear friend, a comrade in battle, and an equal. Outside of that, he is kind and gentle—" charming and sweet... "He would make a perfect candidate for anyone's hand. And to a Kremnoan, he bears much of our own values within himself."

Tenacious, honourable, self-sacrificing... Need the prince go on? Any fair maiden or young warrior would swoon upon his mere gaze, and that radiant smile was honed to put the wary at ease; yet it was not those superficial traits which Mydeimos adored, no. Rather, it was the man he had glimpsed behind that heroic facade; that of a vulnerable, heartbroken soul who had seen far too much, yet still remained determined. There was much to admire about Phainon.

"He is an enigma," Krateros said. "He hails from an unknown land, bears no lineage, and his goals are shrouded in secrecy."

"That matters not." Since when did titles and prestige weigh heavy on a Kremnoan's judgement, anyway?

The old warrior scoffed next, both amused and bemused. "He even had to beg me to teach him how best to communicate with you. He has no concept of our language, let alone our traditions."

Well, that was to be expected. Foreign concepts should bewilder an outsider, just as a chimera would become perplexed upon the sight of a nymph. It was prudent of Phainon to have sought out someone close to Mydeimos in an attempt to learn of their ways.

Oh, and that reminded him, "Have I told you about the time he once personally gifted me a bouquet of flowers?" Laughter snuck through Mydeimos as he recalled that priceless scene. "The look on his face when I explained its meaning..."

"My word..."

"He meant no harm by it." Phainon had merely been issuing his own traditions, was all, "but his reaction will remain in my memory till eternal death."

"Of all the indignity..." Krateros shook his head, much like a disapproving elder who had witnessed a hilarious, blasphemous scene. "And you still deem him a worthy equal—nay, a suitor, Mydeimos?"

What a strange and weighted question. "And what if I do?"

Though Mydeimos did not doubt his feelings for Phainon having grown as a budding flower amidst Kephale's light, there still lied an inkling within him that questioned the true identity of those emotions. Whilst Phainon carried an unceasing, blazing devotion for the prince, Mydeimos felt his own adoration quite lacking. Was it love that stirred in his heart? Was it the same stubborn loyalty he felt as he had for Hephaestion? Would he pledge himself to Phainon?

It was... difficult to say. Therefore, Mydeimos thought it best to let it stew, even if for just a little longer. Such things took time to blossom, and no Kremnoan was quick to bow their head. Mydeimos could only appreciate the immense patience Phainon afforded him, along with the reins the Deliverer had placed on his own temperament.

There was neither a rush nor any pressure to reach a decision. Mydeimos had nearly the gall to prefer it over his looming duties of kingship. At least Phainon made for pleasant company—especially in the early hours of slumber when he donned nothing but an atrocious pairing of a purple chiton and an ichor-yellow sash.

Krateros did not deem the prince's silence to be any affirmation, and he instead shook his head once more and retired the subject.

It was nearly Parting Hour when Phainon next found Mydeimos in the Heroes' Baths. He was stripped of his usual attire, donning only a bathrobe that did poorly to hide the mess he was in. His hair was clumped with redsoil, his skin dirtied with mud, and there were tender imprints on both his cheeks that resembled a dromas' maw.

Regardless of the state of himself, the Deliverer seemed relieved to find Mydeimos as he quickly joined him in the pool. "Ah, Mydei! I see you've been well. Has the feast with your people gone smoothly?"

"It has," the prince answered with a mindless hum. The waters rose up to his chest and splashed about with a floundering fool, yet he merely allowed a smile to sneak upon his lips. "I would ask if anything had happened, but the answer lies in plain sight."

Rather than laughing along to his teasing, however, the Deliverer hissed sharply, freezing amidst the pool as he grit his teeth and raised his arms above the water. "Ahh, that's hot! Mydei... did you turn up the heat again?"

"Of course I did." There wasn't anyone else in the Heroes' Baths, after all? Why wouldn't Mydeimos adjust the temperature to suit his comfort? Wasn't the thick steam wafting about enough of an indication?

It took a moment for Phainon to acclimatise, longer still as he continued to tread through the water as though it were mud. He shuffled nearer to Mydeimos' seat and practically hung his head low in an awfully dramatic groan.

Honestly, what else was the prince to do but splash a handful of hot water upon Phainon's face? "Pitiable Deliverer. No partner of mine shall be incapacitated by a mere bath; nor should they reek of redsoil."

Another terribly miserable groan. What was once exuberance and joy now became glum.

"Professor Anaxa got a bit too excited with feeding the dromas," Phainon huffed and puffed. "Unfortunately, the younglings managed to swarm around the stash, and he tasked me with wrangling them up..."

Oh, how dreadful. Mydeimos chuckled and shook his head. He could picture the scene vividly; a ruckus made into an absolute circus, with the famed Deliverer being accosted by a herd of young dromas. With any luck, news would have spread throughout Okhema by now, and that 'blasphemous' scholar would bear not a single care for either of their reputations.

Regardless, Phainon seemed to be unharmed. A little winded, perhaps, but his complaining bode well.

"A hot bath will do you good, then," Mydeimos said as he waved him over to sit closer. "Come, the water is a fair bit cooler on the edges of the pool."

Phainon sprang right over. The waters rose and crashed upon them as he moved with purpose, settling right by the prince's seat with only a generous distance kept between them.

Odd. Mydeimos craned his head over toward the Deliverer. For as affectionate as Phainon was, he did not dare lay a finger upon him whenever they lounged in the baths. He had always remained careful, as though he feared his advances were too much for Mydeimos.

"What's the matter?" he asked, even if he knew the answer at heart.

Phainon's face had grown a bright flush, the steam wafting up and dampening his hair. The mark on his neck seemed to shimmer as he let out a breathless laugh. "Ah, forgive my caution, but the last time we shared a bath so close..."

Yes, indeed. Phainon had ended up with a punctured lip. But that had been a different issue entirely—memories dragged back up from the depths of Mydeimos' mind and startling him.

"I don't want to impose any more than I already have..." Phainon explained. "You have been far too kind, Mydei, even though my enthusiasm often leads you to discomfort. I suppose... I should learn to control myself a little better."

"Hmph." Still so reserved, yet shameless, was he? Such a dichotomy could only ever be achieved by this fool.

Certainly, it was endearingly kind of the Deliverer to put his partner above his own desires, yet Mydeimos had already allowed his touch outside of the baths. They'd even come to share a bed when the opportunity arose. Did Phainon still carry an iota of guilt?

Perhaps.

The prince pinned him no blame—no one was to blame. Instead, he sighed, and took it upon himself to initiate, albeit hesitantly.

Reaching out had never been his strong suit. A Kremnoan does not seek comfort in the ways others might. Touch, worship... It did not come naturally. It was rarely received well, too, no matter how much a warrior may yearn. Only through hard-forged connections could a Kremnoan ever accept even the slightest praise, for it was through loyalty and faithfulness alone that tethered one's regard.

It shall never be understated, then, just how many times Phainon had earned his keep. Mydeimos saw no harm in his need for affections. In fact, he found it quite... charming. He might liken the Deliverer to an overly enthusiastic and overzealous puppy who thrived off of attention like a Kremnoan does glory.

The prince came closer, glancing upon Phainon for any strange reactions, subtle or not. He dared brush his fingers along his hand under the steaming pool, before he felt the Deliverer's soaked sleeve against his bare arm.

Mydeimos raised his other hand from the water, drawing it up towards Phainon's hair. He brushed through the heavy locks, sweeping it out of his face, nothing more than a tender gesture that set his heart aflame.

"This is fine," he mumbled, an encouragement to appease Phainon into relaxing his tense shoulders. "I will tell you if it's too much, I promise."

And indeed, his touch and words alone seemed to quell the anxieties within the Deliverer's mind, as if that was all he needed to be a little more at ease.

Phainon leaned towards him, seeking more of his touch, and Mydeinos indulged him with the ghost of a smile. The prince tucked a stray lock of hair behind one ear, parted the dampened fringe, grazed his bare fingers along Phainon's scalp till he cupped the base of his skull...

And all the while, a shiver ran through the Deliverer. As though he were a block of ice—more so than he already was—he practically melted right into Mydeimos. Like dust clinging on to him; like sand cupped in his hands. The vibrant blush on Phainon's cheeks spread down his neck as a trembling sound escaped him.

It was... a little strange, but Mydeimos was not perturbed.

"Is this alright?" he wondered.

And he received a rather fervent nod. "Mmm... Mhmm."

Phainon clutched at the prince's bathrobe and tugged. "More, please."

What an endearing sight. Mydeimos found himself quick to oblige. He snuck a fleeting brush along the small of Phainon's back, crawling his fingers over to grip his waist and pulled him to flushed by his side. He welcomed the Deliverer's head to rest against his chest, carding through his hair gently, as if he were parting the waters of their bath.

He could feel every shuddering breath against his robe, how fragile Phainon's body felt—a terribly intimate sensation he had steadily been acclimatised to these past many weeks. The steam rose and clouded the air, filled their lungs with a comforting heat, yet somehow, someway, Phainon retained an inkling of frigidness that made his skin clammy to the touch. Cold vapour blew from every exhale, turning warm as they joined the steam. That odd quirk of his was an interesting thing, yet Mydeimos put it aside in favour of reaching back into the water to squeeze Phainon's hand from where it gripped his robe.

"You needn't restrain yourself."

How strange it was to hear his partner laugh in such a dulcet tone. It was as though his voice had become raspy with some sort of strain, almost delirious in its nature.

"Now... I'm beginning to feel... just as overwhelmed as you," Phainon sighed oh-so deeply between his words.

And what an amusing remark that was. "All the better, then. I find myself wanting to see you more relaxed."

"Then, come'ere..."

As if he had been possessed by some unknown force, the Deliverer suddenly wound his arms around Mydeimos. Water splashed and crashed about, mixing heat with cold, stirring the pot that welled inside them both. Phainon buried his face into his partner's neck, shamelessly swallowing breath after breath as a shudder ran past him.

Enthusiastic and bold, bright and ecstatic. Perhaps Phainon was overjoyed. Not once had Mydeimos reciprocated his advances to this extent before, even in the privacy of their bedchambers. This was foreign territory between them, a precious moment that crossed over a mere language barrier.

Regardless of traditions, culture, or beliefs, it was nice to bring Phainon joy; it was nice to see him wear a genuine smile free of burdens and obligations. It was nice to hold him, feel him, and hear his voice ring. It was nice to recognise his fluttering heartbeat from where he laid flush against Mydeimos.

If only they could indulge for the rest of time. If fate weren't so cruel... If only the prophecy hadn't set their paths toward a predestined end, then this could've been so much sweeter. Still, Mydeimos rid himself of those thoughts before they could fester. Regardless if this was but a fleeting instance, he will treasure it as dearly as he did the man in his arms.

"Wash yourself off," the prince murmured, as though he were waking a slumbering lump having hogged the blanket. He scooped a handful of water and doused Phainon's hair, rinsing some of the redsoil's stain from the pristine snow. "Go on. We can continue once we return to my bedchambers."

"Yours?" came the drowsy mumble, followed by a more delicate, lighter chuckle. "Sure."

Afterwards, once the sun dials had long shifted to signal the Parting Hour, it was through Mydeimos' insistence that brought them out of the pool. The cool air clung to his skin just as much as Phainon. Every step along the stone path leading to the changing rooms cut through the silence that pervaded them.

For some strange, inexplicable reason, Phainon deemed it worth to stick to the prince's side as though he were a lost child. He was ceaseless in his grip, even when Mydeimos attempted to pry him off with the excuse of getting dressed.

"At least take a moment to put on some clothes."

"Hmph."

Incorrigible man. A clingy, petulant fool he was.

Fortunately, Phainon did come to see reason, eventually. The price, however, was a piece of Mydeimos' clothing in place of his embrace; that which ended up being a worn Kremnoan robe the Deliverer swaddled around himself over his own chiton.

Mydeimos shook his head; though he would argue it was to rid some of the water from his hair. At least the bathhouse attendants were quick to provide a spare set of clothes for him. At least Phainon seemed content—more so than the prince had ever seen of him.

He was dazed, as though his head was filled with steam. His robe was worn so poorly that the collar threatened to slip down his shoulder. He hadn't even tied his sash properly, even as a thought managed to connect inside his bath-addled stupor.

"Oh, that reminds me." Something peculiar skewed his expression before he took his partner's hand. "I have somewhere to be. It won't take long. You can go on ahead."

What a strange remark. "What is this all of a sudden?" Was there something amiss?

But the Deliverer merely smiled. He brought Mydeimos' hand up to brush against his cheek.

"It's a surprise," Phainon said, before he nuzzled into the perfect space of the prince's palm. His lashes fluttered in what might be bliss, his eyes becoming dull in such an interesting way, Mydeimos couldn't help but brush his thumb along the cold skin of his cheekbone.

"A surprise, you say? Very well, then." Were he just as clingy, he may have also asked to not take too long. For as lax as his body now was, he felt a slight ache in his heart at the prospect of having to wait. But that was unimportant.

That wide, toothy grin was a fine price to receive. The colour had not left Phainon's cheeks, and all it did was cause the brilliance of his eyes to shimmer like crystalline waters.

Like a doting chimera, Phainon nuzzled into Mydeimos' palm before departing. Time seemed to pass by so much slower then, with each second clearing the pleasant haze which kept the prince's mood up in the clouds. He might liken it to the sensation of sobering up with a bitter drink after a fulfilling sleep, or a splash of ice-cold water over his face. Regardless, it served him no purpose to loiter in the changing rooms, so Mydeimos dragged his sandalled feet up to the quiet wing where the private chambers for the Chrysos Hairs were.

The familiar creek of the doors closed behind him, leaving him to his privacy. The curtains blocked the eternal light, forgotten since the previous day. Stagnant air entered the prince's lungs as he first lit the hearth to chase away the ghost of Phainon's touch.

It warmed him, both the flickering flames and the memory of that smile. How strange. Never had Mydeimos experienced such endearment this... potently, as though he held a burning core of steel in his bare hands. Was this what Phainon felt for him? This... longing; this heavy restlessness. It was not unique, but its intensity was one Mydeimos was quite unused to. He found that he did not hate it.

To wait for a treasured partner to return to his side brought an awfully impatient pang in his heart. To experience it to this extent was almost worrying, as if it had snuck upon the prince without his knowledge. The silence he waited in gave rise to introspection, and fresh memories replayed in his mind like an amateur bard reciting the only verse they knew.

For a while, Mydeimos spent his lonesome with idle tasks, be it leaving his sandals by the doors, or slipping the curtains apart to allow a few thin streaks of light to break the flame-lit darkness. He changed out of his Okheman tunic and into a more comfortable set of worn Kremnoan robes embroidered with flowers and flames. He poured himself a goblet of pomegranate juice, plucked a scroll by his shelf, and lounged on a chaise by the hearth with nary an ounce of tension in his bones.

It was there where Phainon found him, much, much later than one would expect. First came the muffled footsteps from beyond the doors, then the clang of the iron handles, and finally a cotton ball for a head snuck between the gaps before slinking inside.

Phainon hid his hands behind his back. There was a mischievous gleam to his eyes, akin to a fox's fangs emerging from the shadows. The large sleeves of his borrowed robes did well to mask any hints of what he brought.

Mydeimos lowered the scroll to tilt his head, if only for a mild attempt to catch whatever it was in the fool's hands. A slight rustle of metal perked him up, though Phainon did not let the prince stew for too long before he revealed... 

A tray... of honeycakes, drizzled in a sweet-smelling sauce and spread generously in jam. There were grapes and wildberries piled into a bowl, a small dish containing oxygala, and another plate of charred bread.

"Ta-daaa!" A proud exclamation for a proud man, one who smelled of burnt soot and raw batter.

Mydeimos traded his gaze from the dishes to his partner, unable to keep the astonishment from his voice. "Did you just prepare that?"

"I had some help," Phainon admitted. "Lady Aglaea happened to be in the kitchens for a late teatime snack, and she deemed it worth her time to lend a hand. I did prepare the honeycakes all by myself, though."

"I can tell." And now the Deliverer looked to be in need of another bath.

The scroll was wound back and placed upon the table with his drink nearby. Mydeimos rose from his seat and approached the eager fool who merely stared, even as the prince grabbed the hem of his loose, long sleeve and brought it up to the flour smeared across Phainon's cheek.

"I would rather you not dirty my bed," Mydeimos said, and he meant it wholeheartedly. "You smell of the honeycakes you so proudly boast. I take it that you have not only burnt the food?"

"Maybe a little."

What an utter fool.

A thinly-veiled smile graced the prince's face. "Perhaps I'll set aside a day to teach you some basic skills in the kitchen. Come, sit."

And a giddy grin simply bloomed as Phainon followed him to the chaise. "Really? I thought you hate having distractions in the kitchen?"

"I do," and the Deliverer had only ever grown to be more and more distracting, "but I can make an exception."

A teasing remark was set to leave Phainon's lips, but he held his tongue in the end, if only because he was urged to sit by a steady hand pressing down on his shoulder. The tray was taken and set on the table. A hand soon carded through his hair, gentle as a breeze, tender as a sweet, doting kiss.

Mydeimos climbed back to the chaise and joined his partner's side. A kiss... what a forward thought. 

The bowl of grapes and wildberries was passed to him, yet the first bite was not his to take. Rather, the prince tapped a single plump berry against Phainon's lips for a silent offering, and he did not move until he was obliged.

A cold, yet firm, arm snaked around Mydeimos' waist. A curious hum, the batting of snow-dusted lashes, and a pair of eyes brimming with far too many emotions for the prince to decipher prompted him to feed another berry onto Phainon's awaiting tongue. The arm around him tightened, that endearing grin cut through feverish cheeks, a strange sound reverberated as Phainon chewed and swallowed.

Dinner was held just like this, taking turns pushing berries between each other's lips, watching like hawks, smiling like love-drunk youths with no concern for the greater world. It was a bizarre and riveting experience, a pleasant blur of comfort steeped in so much warmth. The more time passed, the more Mydeimos engaged, indulged, and drowned in it, the more he understood what it was Phainon craved with his need for affection. Being smothered in tender love, even as chaste as this, it served to endear the prince ever more. He found that he could not bear to look away.

Perhaps... he could get used to this unfamiliar experience.

"Say 'ahhh'!"

"You are ridiculous," yet, Mydeimos parted his lips to accept the bite of honeycakes fed to him. Sweet syrup coated his tongue, along with a light dusting of sugar. The honeycakes themselves were overcooked, however. One might think that the garnishing was merely a means to hide the gritty, charred edges.

Phainon's body had become a comfortable weight against him. Somewhere along the way, the prince had gradually become cornered, sandwiched between the plush armrest of the chaise and a cold body draped in crimson and gold. The crackling of the hearth, the hue of the fire, along with the golden light streaking from the gaps between the nearby curtains painted a spectacle of colours. The scent of honey permeated the air, the smokiness of the flames, now joined by a newly acquainted note of pinewood.

Later, when the fireplace had begun to calm, did the two men abandon their empty plates and bowls unto the table. With their hands now free, the atmosphere steeped in their hours of intimacy beckoned for the other's touch; to graze their fingers along skin, to hold each other's bodies, to weave through hair... Why, they were but human.

And Mydeimos had much to catch up on. This newfound delight stirring embers in his fiery blood was no different to an addiction. There was no explanation for goosebumps trailing behind Phainon's touch, as he traced the flaming marks from Mydeimos' throat down to his sternum. A shiver ran past the prince, and he tightened his embrace and clung to the fabric of his partner's robe.

To be handled as if he were made of glass was... perplexing. To be gazed upon this closely, this intensely, it was almost overwhelming, like a blinding light piercing through his eyelids. To witness this vulnerable side of Phainon he wouldn't dare reveal to anyone else...

It burned so hot, leaving traces of a tender numbness in its wake. Mydeimos was used to the heat, yet this was on a different scale, something he was wholly unprepared to handle.

"Mydei." A soft whisper breathed against the tips of his hair, and all he could do to respond was grunt.

"You're blushing. No, your markings..."

What of them?

A gentle hand cupped his right cheek. Phainon brushed his thumb over the prince's lashes, tracing the red lining that led to the symbol below his eye.

"You're so warm," the Deliverer mused, "and your markings glow when you feel flustered. Titans, you're beautiful."

Flattery, no more than an unnecessary remark. But Mydeimos was not so oblivious to his partner's devotion to recognise that it was wholeheartedly earnest.

"Phainon." He could hardly speak. The air in his lungs sat heavy and refused to leave his throat, as though his words were blasphemous and lacked any right to be uttered aloud, "This—it's too much."

Mercifully—mercilessly—all of that heaviness and heat, numbness and cold, removed itself at once. The suddenness was akin to a lash of wind, stealing Mydeimos' breath and pitching it to a raspy grumble.

And between their lips—the both of them—came a hushed whisper, "I'm sorry."

His clothes felt much too thick. They clung to his skin through a thin sheen of sweat. Yet, when Mydeimos dared open his eyes, all he found was the same expression mirrored back. Breathless, dishevelled, and addled by devotion.

"I'm sorry, Mydei..." Frost ghosted over the prince's lips as Phainon raised himself on his arms. His brilliant eyes, as bright as clear skies, were shot wide with a different concoction of emotions. His brows were furrowed with worry, twisted with something raw, something... unheard of.

Mydeimos wasn't sure what to make of it, for he was preoccupied with wrangling an ounce of his composure back. His traitorous heart would not slow its race, just as the tempest raging within him refused to calm. His fingertips buzzed as though he had dipped them in freshly spilled blood. His vision trembled, unable to settle on a single point of focus. His tongue sat like iron in his mouth.

"I pushed too far, didn't I?" Phainon asked.

"N-no, no." Curse the way the prince's voice trembled. He had no will to push the Deliverer away, nor did he wish to see that terrible expression sour further with that brooding personality of his.

Thus, did Mydeimos cling tightly unto his partner's robe. He swallowed a dry ball of air to steel his nerves. Since when did this ever become a battle to confront?

"I am just... unused to this, still," he sighed through a haggard breath. "Give it time. I will eventually acclimatise."

"Even so, I shouldn't overwhelm you," Phainon argued.

Oh, but there was no better way than this. It was not the Deliverer's fault for stirring up these unquenchable flames. He meant no harm—he would never dare hurt Mydeimos outside of a spar. They merely clashed, for now. The reasons mattered not.

A gentle, assuring smile graced the prince's face. It was as warm as he could manage, regardless if his words came off unsteadily. "I may not ever be able to match the passion you bear for me, but by Nikador's tenacity, I am willing to try. You, of all people, deserve nothing less. I can think of no one better to share my burdens with, and I would hope you think me more durable than a maiden who has never felt a lover's touch."

"That's... quite the acknowledgement."

"Perhaps so." He merely spoke his mind. If it were anything substantial, then best let it be said now, lest incessant doubts festered once again.

Phainon tipped his head against his shoulder. The ends of his hair grazed along the prince's face, like feathers brushing over him. "But, Mydei, this isn't a competition. There is no need to match my love for you. Whatever you give is more than enough."

Perhaps so, and yet, "What if I want to give you more?"

"It'll always be enough. I will prove it to you, time and time again if need be."

Perhaps. Overzealous, overeager Phainon, who had all the love in the world to give. Why was he hesitant to receive it in kind?

It may be too much. It may burn like fires licking his skin, but Mydeimos would come to endure it, just as he endured most other things. It was just fortunate that this love was due to sweeten in time. He would make sure of it, till it, too, would thaw his partner's heart; until eventually, Phainon would come to see that he was deserving of that same love he gave so freely.

Though time may be a precious resource, not a second would be wasted on such an endeavor. In the months Phainon had endeared himself to Mydeimos, he had also carved a space within the prince's undying heart, a space filled with a myriad of strange, confusing, and enlightening emotions.

A quiet, curious hum sounded as the Deliverer was pulled back to his partner's arms. His body tensed, as though he feared to overstep, but Mydeimos steadied him, held him firm, and stroked along the length of his spine in an effort to comfort.

A cold body wracked with shivers, a pitiful, wistful groan, Phainon turned to putty under the prince's careful touch. Words escaped him, travelling as reverberations against Mydeimos' chest. They were but meaningless noise, conveying only a momentary surrender, an impasse once again shelved for another time.

Perhaps one day, should fate grant them a morsel of a happy ending, there may come a future when Phainon could accept love as easily and readily as he gave it. There would be no fear, no hesitation, no second guessing, no disregard for his own desires... And Mydeimos could not help but find humour in how Phainon alone could stir such a whimsical, naive wish within him, as though the sun he bore had managed to shine through crystalline armour built over years upon years of ceaseless war.

And what was worse? The mere fact that not an ounce of frustration could ever be pointed toward him in response.

chapters.html:
End Notes

The reason this fic is still tagged 'Developing Relationship' is because Mydeimos is oblivious about love. He sees Phainon's devotion towards him and compares it to his own admiration for Phainon and thinks, "Maybe I'm not in love yet. Phainon is pretty passionate for me, while I don't feel that same intensity in return. I'll give it more time."

The lion does not understand emotions, for he all he knows is wet. He is, however, still more emotionally secure than Phainon.
